did_you_know.text: The ark was placed in the tent David had prepared for it, and burnt offerings and fellowship offerings were presented before the LORD on that occasion.
David gave every man and woman in Israel a portion of food, thereby involving the entire nation in the joy of bringing the ark.
David appointed Levites to minister before the ark by commemorating, giving thanks, and praising the LORD, the God of Israel.
Asaph was appointed leader of the musicians and played the cymbals, while other Levites played harps and lyres.
Benaiah and Jahaziel, the priests, blew the trumpets before the ark of God’s covenant; this is described as a regular ministry.
On the day the ark was brought, David gave Asaph and his fellow Levites a song of thanks, thereby establishing the beginning of musical worship before the ark.
The song of thanks reminds Israel that they are Jacob’s descendants and God’s chosen ones, emphasizing that they must remember the LORD’s wonders and judgments.
The song describes God’s covenant with Jacob and Israel as an everlasting covenant and connects it with the promise of the land of Canaan.
The song addresses not only Israel but the whole earth and all nations, calling them to proclaim the LORD’s salvation and declare his glory.

After the celebration, the responsibilities for worship were divided between two centers: Asaph and his fellow Levites remained to minister before the ark, while Zadok and the priests served at the LORD’s tabernacle in Gibeon.
